name: Hofburg Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Imperial Hofburg in Innsbruck enchants as a Habsburg palace featuring the monumental Giant's Hall, Empress Sisi's apartments, and Rococo splendor.
preis: Adults approx. €10.50, concessions €8.00, youth under 19 free (free with Innsbruck Card)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Imperial Hofburg in Innsbruck on Rennweg stands alongside the Vienna Hofburg and Schönbrunn Palace as one of the three primary imperial residences of Austria. This monumental baroque palace bears eloquent witness to centuries of Habsburg rule in Tyrol. Originally constructed as a late medieval castle under Archduke Sigmund and Emperor Maximilian I, the grand four-wing palace complex owes its present Rococo grandeur to Empress Maria Theresa, who comprehensively redesigned the palace in the 18th century in the Viennese Court style. With its stuccowork, silk wall hangings, and imperial staterooms, the Hofburg mesmerizes cultural travelers from around the world. Together with the Golden Roof and the Court Church, the palace forms the historic heart of the Tyrolean provincial capital.

Route & Requirements

The tour leads visitors through lavishly appointed imperial reception and residential apartments. The undisputed centerpiece is the monumental, two-story Giant's Hall (Riesensaal): this 31-meter-long banquet hall features vibrant ceiling frescoes by Franz Anton Maulbertsch and monumental portraits of the imperial family, showing Maria Theresa, her consort Francis Stephen of Lorraine, and their 16 children. Other prominent highlights include the Guard Room, the Lorraine Chamber, and the Empress Elisabeth Apartments adorned with period furnishings of the beloved Empress Sisi. Archival portraits, crystal chandeliers, and decorative arts vividly illustrate the courtly splendor of Habsburg Innsbruck. The baroque Court Chapel was founded by Maria Theresa following the sudden demise of Emperor Francis Stephen in 1765 as a memorial sanctuary. All exhibition galleries are fully accessible and accompanied by multi-language audio guides.

Visit & Arrival

The Hofburg is open daily year-round from 09:00 to 17:00. Admission is €10.50 for adults, €8.00 reduced; children and adolescents under 19 enjoy free entry. Entry is included free with the Innsbruck Card. Reaching the palace: from Innsbruck Central Station, walk 10 minutes through the old town; trams and city buses stop at Museumsstraße or Congress. By car: autobahn exit Innsbruck Ost or Mitte, with parking at the Congressgarage or Altstadtgarage.

Tips

Make good use of the audio guide included with admission for fascinating insights into Habsburg dynasty history. Following your palace visit, stroll through the neighboring Hofgarten with its shaded avenues and historic music pavilion. Stop into the famous Café Sacher directly in the Hofburg complex for authentic original Sachertorte. Visiting during morning hours guarantees a tranquil museum experience.
